sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: The European wild apple is a small deciduous tree or shrub reaching about 10 m. It grows in European woods and woodland edges; identification is complicated by hybridisation with cultivated apple.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The flowers are about 2–3 cm across. The small apples are usually yellow-green and sometimes blushed by the sun, about 2–3 cm in diameter.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The tart fruits are edible and can be cooked. A horticultural source recommends removing the pips; tartness should not be confused with toxicity.
